tickets.title: Wire dot-repeat and macro record/playback into the production coordinator
tickets.status_note: 2026-09-17 discovery while pursuing T045 (G3 qualification, whose E01 acceptance names 'dot' explicitly): the production CLI's Vim dispatcher (packages/workbench/vim-session/index.ts, 1594 lines, no match for 'Repeat', 'dot' or 'Macro') never calls any of packages/vim/src/index.ts's repeat API (applyVimRepeatEvent, createVimInsertRepeatTarget, createVimOperatorRepeatTarget, createVimRepeatState, recordVimRepeatTarget, replayVimMultiDot) or macro API. T024 ('Implement semantic dot repeat', done) and T025 ('Implement macro recording and execution', done) both explicitly and honestly disclaimed this in their own evidence Limitations sections ('The workbench/parser dispatcher must wire successful native command outcomes to applyVimRepeatEvent...downstream owner work' / '...connect q/@ parser intents to the recording and execution APIs; command wiring...remain downstream owner work') — those tickets are not mis-scoped, but no ticket was ever created to do the downstream wiring itself, and it does not exist. Reproduced twice with real production PTY sessions, byte-exact: (1) dot-repeat: 'gg0x' deletes the first character of line 1 correctly, then 'j0.j0.' on lines 2/3 leaves them completely unchanged — dot-repeat is a total no-op in production despite T080's multi-cursor semantics being fully unit-tested. (2) macros: 'qax' 'q' (record register a: delete first char) then 'j0@a' (play it on line 2) leaves the ENTIRE file byte-for-byte unchanged, including no visible effect from the 'x' typed while ostensibly recording — macro record/playback does not execute at all in production. Ordinary motions/operators/Insert/Visual/Ex commands are confirmed working correctly through the same dispatcher (ciw, o, undo, :w/:wq all verified byte-exact in the same sessions), so this is a precisely scoped gap, not a general dispatcher failure. This blocks T045's E01 acceptance ('...ciw, dot...') and full G2/G3 Vim-correctness claims; do not mark T045 done until this closes with a real production PTY proof of '.' repeat and 'q'/'@' macro playback matching Neovim-oracle semantics. Separately fixed (2026-09-17, under T038's maintenance per AGENTS.md since T038 owns packages/workbench/): a related but distinct bug found in the same investigation, where bare 'q' in Normal mode (Xi's documented quick-quit shortcut) silently discarded unsaved edits because it bypassed the dirty-buffer check ':q' already enforces. Fixed by routing it through the same submitCommandLine('q') path; see docs/evidence/T038.md's 2026-09-17 addendum. That fix is unrelated to and does not reduce the remaining scope of this ticket (dot-repeat and macro record/playback are still completely unwired in production). 2026-09-17 (later same day): implemented and wired dot-repeat ('.') into the production dispatcher (packages/workbench/vim-session/index.ts) for the single-cursor delete-operator+motion/text-object and plain-insert cases T024 already models and oracle-tested; verified with a new production PTY test (tests/e2e/t130-dot-repeat-pty.py, 3/3 clean runs, 7 cases: operator repeat, insert repeat, repeated dot, no-target no-op, Ctrl-C non-recording, direct-change-key non-target). See docs/evidence/T130.md. 2026-09-17 (later same day): implemented and wired macro record/playback. Playback ('@'/'@@') and stop-recording (bare 'q' while already recording) use their real, unmodified Vim keys with zero conflict, via T025's already oracle-tested executeVimMacro. Starting a recording uses a new leader-key trigger ('<space>q<register>') instead of bare 'q'+register, because bare 'q' alone is already Xi's own documented, shipped quick-quit shortcut (docs/evidence/T038.md) extensively relied upon across dozens of existing tests and T094's own evidence; removing that shipped behavior to make room for the literal Vim trigger was judged out of scope for a ticket whose job is 'wire the existing tested engine in', not 'redesign a shipped keybinding'. Verified with a new production PTY test (tests/e2e/t130-macro-pty.py, 4/4 clean runs, 6 cases: quit-shortcut regression checks unchanged, invalid-register safety, record+replay, @@ repeat-last, counted replay). Full regression clean: bun run check, test:e2e --suite interaction 39/39, every other e2e/distribution fixture individually, test:ui 7/7, test:unit 31/31, test:services 28/28, the underlying T024/T025/T080/T092/T033 engine tests, two bench/performance harnesses, plan.py check.
